title: White House Spanish-Language Website and X Profile Taken Offline in 2025
description_short: White House Spanish-Language Website and X Profile Taken Offline in 2025
description_medium: Within hours of Donald Trump’s January 20, 2025 inauguration, the Spanish-language White House website was taken offline and showed a 404 error. An Associated Press report republished by PBS NewsHour also identified the White House’s Spanish-language X profile, @LaCasaBlanca, and a government reproductive-freedom page as disbanded. A White House spokesperson said the site was being edited and said the Spanish translation section would return; the report gave no restoration date.
description_long:
At about 4 p.m. Eastern on January 20, 2025, hours after Donald Trump’s inauguration, the Spanish versions of the White House website and social media accounts became unavailable, according to TrumpFile’s timeline. The Associated Press, in a report republished by PBS NewsHour, said the new administration took down the Spanish-language White House website; the site returned an “Error 404” message. The report named the White House’s Spanish-language X profile, @LaCasaBlanca, and the government page on reproductive freedom as also disbanded. It noted that Spanish pages for the Departments of Labor, Justice, and Agriculture remained available on Tuesday.

Asked about the change on the administration’s second day, principal deputy press secretary Harrison Fields said the White House was developing, editing, and tweaking its website, and that some archived content had gone dormant. He said the administration was committed to bringing the Spanish translation section back online and reloading dormant content “in a short timeline,” without specifying when. The contemporaneous reporting documents the initial outage and the administration’s stated plan; it does not establish a later restoration date or whether every affected page or account returned. The record therefore describes assets taken offline during the transition rather than a proven permanent shutdown.
